:::{#exr-residual-variance-more-covariates}
#### Condition on one more covariate

Let $\Predvar$ and $Z$ be [covariates](#def-covariate) of one [observation](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-observation) from a [population](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-population),
and let $\Outvar$ be its [outcome](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-outcome), with $\E{\Outvar^2} < \infty$.
The [residual variance](#def-irreducible-error) given $\Predvar$, averaged over the covariate values, is $\E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}$.
Measuring the further covariate $Z$ replaces it by $\E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar, Z}}$.
Comparing the two says whether measuring $Z$ can shrink the part of the outcome that no [prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) removes.

::: {.callout-tip title="Hint"}
Apply the [law of total variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-total-variance) [conditional](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-cond-expectation) on $\Predvar = \predvar$,
with $Z$ in the role of the conditioning variable,
and then average over $\Predvar$ with the [law of iterated expectations](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-lie).
:::

Show that

$$
\E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}
= \E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar, Z}} + \E{\Var{\E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar, Z} \mid \Predvar}}.
$$

:::
